Script.name: MuddlerReload
Script.script:
-- Hot-reload companion for FieryDev profile. -- -- Watches the repo's `.output` JSON pointer (written by -- Muddler in -w mode). When it changes, uninstall + -- reinstall FierymudRs from the path the pointer names. -- -- The repo lives in WSL2; Mudlet runs on Windows. The -- normal `addFileWatch` path uses Qt's QFileSystemWatcher, -- which on Windows watches local paths via -- ReadDirectoryChangesW and falls back to polling for -- remote paths. UNC into the WSL filesystem -- (`\\wsl.localhost\...`) reports as remote but in -- practice doesn't deliver change events at all, so we -- run our own mtime poll on top.
MuddlerReload = MuddlerReload or {} local M = MuddlerReload
-- The repo path is per-machine — for WSL2 devs it's a UNC -- like `//wsl.localhost/<distro>/...`, for native Linux/Mac -- devs it's a plain absolute path. Resolution order: -- 1. `<mudlet profile>/MuddlerReload.path` — single-line -- text file containing the path (no quoting). Highest -- priority; lets each profile point at its own repo. -- 2. The fallback baked in below — only useful on the -- original dev's machine; everyone else should set the -- `.path` file. local function readPathConfig() local path = (getMudletHomeDir():gsub("\\", "/")) .. "/MuddlerReload.path" local f = io.open(path, "r") if not f then return nil end local body = f:read("*a") or "" f:close() body = body:gsub("[\r\n%s]+$", ""):gsub("^[%s]+", "") if body == "" then return nil end return body end
M.repoPath = readPathConfig() or [[//wsl.localhost/Ubuntu-24.04/home/strider/Code/mud/FierymudMudletClient]] M.outputPath = M.repoPath .. "/.output" M.pollInterval = 2.0 -- Stat fingerprint of the mpackage from the last poll. We -- stat the *mpackage*, not `.output`, because Muddler writes -- the same 63-byte JSON pointer to `.output` on every build — -- the bytes don't change between builds, only the file -- mtime does. Mpackage size + mtime are reliable change -- signals. M.lastStat = nil
local function debugLog(msg) cecho("\n<cyan>[MuddlerReload]<reset> " .. tostring(msg) .. "\n") debugc("[MuddlerReload] " .. tostring(msg)) end
-- io.open + tell isn't enough to get a real mtime, and -- lfs isn't always available in Mudlet builds. Hash the -- file body instead: the .output JSON is < 100 bytes, so -- the read cost is trivial and any rebuild produces a -- string-distinct value (path or name changes) — except -- in the degenerate "same bytes, different timestamp" -- case, which doesn't happen here because Muddler -- writes a fresh pointer each build. local function readOutputBody() local f = io.open(M.outputPath, "r") if not f then return nil, "cannot open " .. M.outputPath end local raw = f:read("*a") f:close() if not raw or raw == "" then return nil, "empty .output" end return raw end
local function parseOutput(raw) local ok, info = pcall(yajl.to_value, raw) if not ok or type(info) ~= "table" then return nil, "yajl parse failed" end if not info.name or not info.path then return nil, "missing name/path" end return info end
function M:reload() local raw, err = readOutputBody() if not raw then debugLog("read failed: " .. tostring(err)) return end local info, perr = parseOutput(raw) if not info then debugLog("parse failed: " .. tostring(perr)) return end local pkgPath = (M.repoPath .. info.path):gsub("\\", "/") debugLog("reload " .. info.name .. " from " .. pkgPath) pcall(uninstallPackage, info.name) tempTimer(0.3, function() local ok = installPackage(pkgPath) if ok then debugLog("<green>installed " .. info.name .. "<reset>") else debugLog("<red>installPackage returned false for " .. pkgPath .. "<reset>") end end) end
-- Stat the mpackage. Uses lfs (shipped with Mudlet) to -- read modification time + size; returns a concatenated -- fingerprint string that changes on any file write. local function statFingerprint(path) if not lfs or not lfs.attributes then return nil end local ok, attr = pcall(lfs.attributes, path) if not ok or type(attr) ~= "table" then return nil end return tostring(attr.modification) .. ":" .. tostring(attr.size) end
local function mpackagePathFromOutput() local raw, err = readOutputBody() if not raw then return nil, err end local info, perr = parseOutput(raw) if not info then return nil, perr end return (M.repoPath .. info.path):gsub("\\", "/") end
-- Poll-based change detection. First call sets the baseline -- and does NOT reload (that's M:reload's job, called once -- from M:start). Subsequent calls compare fingerprints and -- fire reload when they differ. local function pollOnce() local path = mpackagePathFromOutput() if not path then return end local stat = statFingerprint(path) if not stat then return end if M.lastStat == nil then M.lastStat = stat return end if stat ~= M.lastStat then M.lastStat = stat M:reload() end end
function M:start() M:stop() -- Baseline fingerprint so the first poll doesn't re-fire -- reload on top of the initial install below. local p = mpackagePathFromOutput() M.lastStat = p and statFingerprint(p) or nil -- tempTimer with the third arg `true` makes it repeat -- forever — the previous chained one-shot version silently -- died after a handful of fires. M.pollTimer = tempTimer(M.pollInterval, pollOnce, true) -- Initial sync: install whatever the current .output -- points at. Handles the first-run case where the profile -- only has the companion present. M:reload() debugLog("polling " .. tostring(p) .. " every " .. M.pollInterval .. "s") end
function M:stop() if M.pollTimer then killTimer(M.pollTimer) M.pollTimer = nil end end
local ok, err = pcall(function() M:start() end) if not ok then cecho(string.format( "\n<red>[MuddlerReload] failed to start: %s<reset>\n", tostring(err) )) end
-- --------------------------------------------------------------- -- Remote Lua exec channel -- --------------------------------------------------------------- -- Lets an external driver (e.g. scripts/mock_mud.py over GMCP) -- push arbitrary Lua at this Mudlet instance and read the -- result back. The mock daemon emits `gmcp Test.Exec {id, code}` -- and listens for `Test.Result {id, ok, result, error, printed}`. -- -- Lives in MuddlerReload (not FierymudRs) so it works even when -- the product package is uninstalled or mid-reload — exactly -- when remote diagnostics matter most.
local function handleTestExec() local frame = gmcp and gmcp.Test and gmcp.Test.Exec if type(frame) ~= "table" then return end local id = frame.id or "" local code = frame.code or "" local reply = function(t) t.id = id; sendGMCP("Test.Result", t) end if code == "" then reply({ok=false, error="empty code"}); return end
-- Try as expression (so `getPackages()` returns the table), -- fall back to statement (so `installPackage(...)` runs). local fn, perr = loadstring("return " .. code) if not fn then fn, perr = loadstring(code) end if not fn then reply({ok=false, error=tostring(perr)}); return end
-- Capture print() output so `print(x)` in the exec body -- surfaces in the response instead of vanishing into the -- main console. local printed = {} local oldPrint = print _G.print = function(...) local args = {...} local parts = {} for i = 1, select("#", ...) do parts[i] = tostring(args[i]) end printed[#printed + 1] = table.concat(parts, "\t") end local ok, result = pcall(fn) _G.print = oldPrint
if not ok then reply({ok=false, error=tostring(result), printed=printed}) return end
-- Stringify result. Tables get yajl-encoded so the driver -- side can JSON-decode them; primitives go through tostring. local resultStr if type(result) == "table" then local jok, j = pcall(yajl.to_string, result) resultStr = jok and j or tostring(result) else resultStr = tostring(result) end reply({ok=true, result=resultStr, printed=printed}) end
registerNamedEventHandler("MuddlerReload", "Test.Exec", "gmcp.Test.Exec", handleTestExec)
-- --------------------------------------------------------------- -- Text-trigger fallback: MREXEC then id then code -- --------------------------------------------------------------- -- Inbound GMCP routing to handlers proved unreliable for custom -- packages (Test.Exec never fired even when the package was -- confirmed loaded). The text-trigger path is bulletproof: the -- daemon sends a raw line like `MREXEC:abc123:return 1+1\r\n`, -- this trigger fires regardless of GMCP routing, runs the code -- locally, and sends the result back as outbound GMCP (which we -- know works — Core.Hello and other client → server frames go -- through fine). The daemon catches `MRResult` and correlates -- by id. -- -- Kill any prior trigger from a previous reinstall before -- creating a new one — tempRegexTrigger ids leak across reinstalls -- otherwise and produce duplicate executions per line. if MuddlerReload.execTriggerId then pcall(killTrigger, MuddlerReload.execTriggerId) MuddlerReload.execTriggerId = nil end
local function handleMRExec() local id = matches[2] or "" local code = matches[3] or "" -- Mudlet's sendGMCP takes a single string: "Package.Name body". -- Encode the table as JSON ourselves and concatenate. Earlier -- attempt with sendGMCP("Pkg", table) errored "bad argument #2". local reply = function(t) t.id = id local jok, j = pcall(yajl.to_string, t) if jok then sendGMCP("MRResult " .. j) end end if code == "" then reply({ok = false, error = "empty code"}); return end
-- Destructive ops (uninstallPackage / installPackage / resetProfile) -- are unsafe inside a trigger callback: Mudlet tears down state -- (scripts, timers, editor view, etc.) while the trigger's stack -- frame is still active above. On 4.20.1 this manifests as a -- process crash; on dev branch it's a use-after-free -- (TriggerUnit::uninstall does a synchronous delete on the -- trigger that's currently executing). -- -- Defer the call via tempTimer so the trigger callback finishes -- and the stack unwinds before the destructive work begins. The -- response goes out NOW (synchronous-feeling from the driver's -- side); the action happens ~50ms later. local destructive = code:match("uninstallPackage") or code:match("installPackage") or code:match("resetProfile") if destructive then reply({ok = true, result = "deferred", deferred = true}) tempTimer(0.05, function() local fn, perr = loadstring(code) if not fn then return end pcall(fn) end) return end
local fn, perr = loadstring("return " .. code) if not fn then fn, perr = loadstring(code) end if not fn then reply({ok = false, error = tostring(perr)}); return end
local printed = {} local oldPrint = print _G.print = function(...) local parts = {} for i = 1, select("#", ...) do parts[i] = tostring(select(i, ...)) end printed[#printed + 1] = table.concat(parts, "\t") end local ok, result = pcall(fn) _G.print = oldPrint
if not ok then reply({ok = false, error = tostring(result), printed = printed}) return end
local resultStr if type(result) == "table" then local jok, j = pcall(yajl.to_string, result) resultStr = jok and j or tostring(result) elseif result ~= nil then resultStr = tostring(result) end reply({ok = true, result = resultStr, printed = printed}) end
MuddlerReload.execTriggerId = tempRegexTrigger("^MREXEC:([^:]+):(.+)$", handleMRExec) cecho("\n<magenta>[MuddlerReload]<reset> MREXEC trigger armed (id=" .. tostring(MuddlerReload.execTriggerId) .. ")\n")
-- Connection ready beacon. Fires on script install AND on every -- sysConnectionEvent so the test daemon learns about reconnects -- without polling. Sent as outbound GMCP "MRReady" with a small -- payload describing the install. Daemon broadcasts this to ctrl -- subscribers as a `mudlet_ready` event. local function announceReady(reason) local payload = { reason = reason or "load", version = "0.9.0", time = os.time(), } local jok, j = pcall(yajl.to_string, payload) if jok then pcall(sendGMCP, "MRReady " .. j) end end -- Initial beacon: small delay so the GMCP socket negotiation is -- guaranteed complete before we send. tempTimer(0.6, function() announceReady("install") end) -- Reconnect beacon: every time Mudlet finishes connecting to the -- server (autoreconnect or manual Reconnect), re-announce. registerNamedEventHandler("MuddlerReload", "mr.ready.onConnect", "sysConnectionEvent", function() tempTimer(0.3, function() announceReady("reconnect") end) end)
